name: Grafton Bridge
facts: Grafton Bridge, opened in April 1910, once boasted the world’s largest reinforced concrete arch, spanning 97.6 metres and rising 43 metres above Grafton Gully, a feat that earned it the nickname "Myers' Folly."

In 2009, a $7 million carbon‑fiber upgrade lifted the bridge’s load capacity from 13 to 40 tonnes, enabling it to carry up to 1,200 bus trips daily as part of Auckland’s Central Connector bus‑priority corridor.

The bridge’s original 1910 design incorporated false piers that mimicked classical masonry, yet the true strength lay in the thin vertical members of the concrete arch, a pioneering engineering approach of its era.
